title: The hypervisor SSH key and Proxmox token were stored in clear in the Controller's data directory
description:
The Controller sealed its other secrets with the master key (Consul, ACME, log forwarding, SSO, HA, the UI TLS key), but wrote a hypervisor's libvirt SSH private key (`hypervisors/<id>/ssh.key`) and its Proxmox API token (`hypervisors/<id>/token`) as plaintext (0600). The `-master-key-file` promise - keep it outside the data directory so a copy of the data holds nothing usable - did not hold for these two files, so a volume snapshot or a copy of the data directory gave an attacker the ability to create and destroy VMs on the configured hypervisors.

**Affected**: a Controller with a configured hypervisor, whose data directory can be copied or snapshotted.

**Fix**: the hypervisor store now seals the SSH key and the token with the master key (purposes `hypervisor/<id>/ssh` and `hypervisor/<id>/token`); a file written in clear before this is read and re-sealed in place when it is loaded.

**Besides updating**: nothing - existing hypervisor secrets are re-sealed on the first start after updating.
